items.note: The chips of ds-autocomplete and ds-multi-select now render inside a <span class="chip-row"> instead of sitting directly in the trigger. LAYOUT IS UNCHANGED: outside the new fit mode the wrapper is display:contents, so it adds no box and the chips remain flex items of the trigger exactly as before — spacing, wrapping and height are identical, and nothing needs doing if you never styled the chips from outside. WHAT BREAKS is a CSS override that walks the structure: any selector using the direct-child combinator from the trigger to a chip (`.autocomplete-trigger > ds-tag`, `ds-multi-select .trigger > ds-tag`, and `:first-child`/`:last-child`/`:nth-child` written against the trigger's children) now matches nothing or matches the wrapper. ACTION: drop the combinator (`.autocomplete-trigger ds-tag`) or insert `.chip-row`. Positional selectors should target `.chip-row > ds-tag:first-child` — note the chips are no longer siblings of the filter input, the addon slots or the chevron, so `ds-tag + .autocomplete-input` style adjacency is gone with no replacement. Chips also carry a `data-chip` attribute and the '+N more' marker a `data-chip-overflow` attribute; both are how the width measurement finds them, so do not strip them, but they are fine to select on.

This release's class-member-collision entry, the counterpart of 0.8.0's and 0.9.0's: it covers every exported class whose member surface changed, so a consumer who EXTENDS a DS component resolves them in one pass. Subclassing a DS component is unsupported (design-system.md), but where it happens the names collide and the build stops: TS4114 demands `override`, TS2415 fires on a redeclared private. WHAT GAINED MEMBERS: AutocompleteComponent and MultiSelectComponent each gained `fitsChipsToWidth`, `chipRow` and `chipsThatFit` — the three fields behind maxVisibleChips="fit". No member was removed and no signature changed. ACTION: rename the subclass's own member, or add `override` if the base's semantics genuinely match. Consumers who only use the <ds-...> elements in templates need no change.

The rule constraining ds-auth-layout's projected [brand] slot no longer declares `width: auto` — only the `max-height` it shipped with in 0.9.0. That declaration sat at specificity (0,2,0), so it out-ranked a width the consumer set on their own logo, and with the slot's default `max-height: none` it achieved nothing: an with no CSS width already keeps its aspect ratio under a max-height. ACTION: none for almost everyone. You are affected ONLY if you both opted into `--ds-auth-layout-brand-max-height` AND set an explicit width on the element you project into [brand] — that logo scaled to keep its ratio before and will now honour your width, i.e. it can squash. Add `width: auto` to your own logo rule to restore the old result. ds-sidenav's identical slot gained the same max-height constraint in this release and deliberately does NOT carry width: auto either, so the two match.

ds-tabs' urlParam now SLUGS a tab's label for the query parameter instead of using it raw. A tab that declares no `value` used to put its display string into the address - ?tab=License%20Verification%20Status - and now yields ?tab=license-verification-status (kebab, lowercased, diacritics decomposed and dropped; a label with nothing sluggable in it, CJK or bare punctuation, keeps its raw text). WHO IS AFFECTED: only consumers who adopted urlParam in 0.9.0 AND left `value` off their ds-tab elements. Their existing links stop matching and land on the first tab, which is what a stale bookmark has always done - nothing throws. ACTION: either accept the new parameter values, or declare `value` on each ds-tab to pin the names permanently, which is the better fix regardless: a slug is still derived from display copy, so renaming a tab still moves the link. NOT CHANGED: tabClosed still emits the raw label, because a host matches it against its own list - the two identifiers are deliberately different now, and the docs said they were the same until this release.

ds-modal and ds-modal-card replace `error: boolean` with `status: DsStatus` ('info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error'), because a boolean cannot express a warning or an info dialog and the rest of the library settled on that vocabulary in 0.9.0. MECHANICAL MAPPING, no judgement needed: [error]="true" becomes status="error"; a bare `error` attribute becomes status="error"; [error]="false" and any unset case become nothing at all (unset is neutral and renders exactly as today); a COMPUTED [error]="expr" becomes [status]="expr && 'error'" - the input accepts false and undefined as "no status", so the shorter && form binds under strictTemplates; [status]="expr ? 'error' : null" is equally correct. ALSO CHANGED, and worth knowing before you look at a screenshot: a status now drives four things rather than one - the icon-badge tint, the title colour, a DEFAULT icon (error/warn/success/info) and the ARIA role, where error and warning make the dialog an `alertdialog`. Both the icon and the role are overridable: `icon` beats the status's pick, an explicit `dialogRole` beats the status's role. The default icon is deliberate, not decoration - a tint on its own signals by colour alone.

CHANGED DEFAULT, visual: maxVisibleChips on ds-autocomplete and ds-multi-select now defaults to "fit" instead of null. A multi-value trigger used to grow a line per selection and push the rest of the form down the page; it now keeps as many chips as it is wide and collapses the rest into '+N more', re-splitting on resize. ACTION: nothing, unless a screen relied on the growth - then bind [maxVisibleChips]="null" to show every chip again. A NUMBER still caps at exactly that many, unchanged. CHECK: a form where a trigger sits above other fields, and any layout whose height was measured or asserted with several chips selected.

The ultra-compact density tier now also compresses --ds-container-pad, the inner padding ds-card and ds-stat share, from 24px (--space-6) to 16px (--space-4). WHO IS AFFECTED: only screens that set [data-density="ultra-compact"] on a container that holds a ds-card or ds-stat. The default and the other three tiers (compact, cozy, comfy) are untouched and still resolve to 24px, so an app that never opts into ultra-compact sees no change. WHY: the tier already compressed field padding and table-cell padding, so a card kept its full 24px frame while its own cells halved - the surface padding was the one it missed. ACTION, if you want the old value inside an ultra-compact container: re-declare --ds-container-pad: var(--space-6) on it. If instead you have per-component pins (--ds-card-pad or --ds-stat-pad) set to work around the shared default, they still win and are unaffected - but consider collapsing them into one --ds-container-pad at :root, which is the lever both components default to.

The size input on fourteen controls (ds-button, ds-icon-button, ds-input, ds-textarea, ds-select, ds-autocomplete, ds-search, ds-date-picker, ds-time-picker, ds-number-stepper, ds-checkbox, ds-radio, ds-switch, ds-field-group) is now typed DsSize | null and defaults to null, so an unbound size can fall through to the new DS_CONFIG.control.size. NOTHING CHANGES IN A TEMPLATE: size="sm" binds exactly as before, and a control with no size still renders md. WHAT CHANGES is reading the signal back - size() returns null when nothing was bound, where it returned 'md' before. ACTION: if you read a control instance's size() (from a host component, a viewChild, or a test assertion), read the public sizeResolved() instead; it returns the same DsSize the component renders at. The same nullable-plus-resolver shape now applies to ds-card elevation (elevationResolved), ds-icon size (sizeResolved) and ds-badge withDot (withDotResolved), and to ds-table bordered / stickyScrollbar. SEPARATELY: if you implement DsFieldGroupContext yourself, its member is now sizeResolved rather than size.

informational: ds-autocomplete and ds-multi-select cap their chips by MEASURED width: one line holds as many as the trigger is wide and the rest collapse into '+N more', re-split whenever the trigger resizes. This is now the DEFAULT (see the chips-cap-by-width-by-default item) - [maxVisibleChips]="null" restores "show everything" and a NUMBER still caps at exactly that many. Choose by what has to stay predictable: a number pins the trigger's HEIGHT whatever the width, "fit" pins the width and lets the count move.

The measurement behind maxVisibleChips="fit" reads the TRIGGER's width, never the chip row's own - a row cannot measure a box whose size the cut changes. Widths are cached per selection and a geometry guard skips re-measuring when neither width nor count moved, so a page of pickers measures once, not once per chip. [maxVisibleChips]="null" opts out of measuring entirely.

DELETE-LIST: if you wrote a ResizeObserver, a container query or a hand-tuned per-breakpoint maxVisibleChips number to keep a chip trigger on one line -> maxVisibleChips="fit" replaces it, and it re-splits on any width change rather than at the breakpoints you listed.

DELETE-LIST: if you capped a chip trigger's height with max-height plus overflow:hidden to stop it growing a line per selection -> that clips a chip mid-glyph and hides the count; maxVisibleChips (a number, or "fit") drops whole chips and reports how many are hidden.

ds-sidenav's brand row fixes, none of which need action: an astral first character (emoji, rarer CJK) no longer paints as tofu in the letter-mark; the mark is aria-hidden, so a screen reader reads the wordmark once instead of announcing the glyph then the name; and a logoLetter set WITHOUT a brand string now renders its tile at all, where an outer gate used to drop the whole lockup.

DELETE-LIST: if you constrained a logo projected into ds-sidenav's [brand] slot with your own max-height (or a wrapper sized to hold it) -> --ds-sidenav-brand-max-height now does it, defaulting to none so nothing changes until you set it.

env(safe-area-inset-*) reads 0 unless YOUR index.html sets viewport-fit=cover in its viewport meta — a notched device alone is not enough, and this library cannot set it for you. ds-auth-layout pads by all four insets and ds-bottom-sheet by the bottom one, so both are plain-padded until you opt in; the docs site now sets it and both component pages state it. ds-bottom-sheet's env() also gained the `, 0px` fallback its siblings had: an unknown env() variable invalidates the entire declaration, which would have taken that sheet's horizontal padding with it.

ds-select, ds-multi-select and ds-autocomplete panels now resolve --ds-dropdown-panel-radius, defaulting to the --ds-radius-panel role so nothing moves until you set it. This is the lever 0.9.0 notes promised as --ds-select-panel-radius, which never existed - that note is corrected in migrations/0.9.0.json. Deliberately panel-level rather than per-component: retuning ONE picker is not a thing the library encourages, and --ds-radius-panel moves modal, popover and date-picker with it. Scope it with a selector - ds-select { --ds-dropdown-panel-radius: 8px } - and only that panel moves, since the token is forwarded onto the portaled pane.

DELETE-LIST: if you wrote a global rule against .ds-dropdown-panel or .cdk-overlay-pane to change a dropdown corner -> --ds-dropdown-panel-radius does it, and scopes to one picker when written under a component selector.

A single-select ds-autocomplete no longer keeps the text typed to filter. Since 0.9.0 that text was also INVISIBLE - the filter input collapses to zero width once a chosen label is on show - while it still narrowed the list, so reopening a settled picker offered one option of four with nothing on screen to explain it. Cleared now whenever the panel closes over a displayed label, which covers both picking and dismissing after typing over a settled value. Multi-select is unchanged on purpose: its input never collapses, so the text stays visible and useful for the next pick. No action - query was component-private and could not be reset from an app.

DELETE-LIST: if you queried a ds-autocomplete inner <input> and dispatched a synthetic input event to clear leftover filter text after a pick -> the component clears it itself now, and clear() has been public since 0.9.0 for emptying value and text together.

The global .link class now resets a <button>: appearance, padding, border, background, font-family, font-size, line-height and text-align. It was written for anchors and touched none of them, yet ds-button warns variant="text" off in favour of .link and an action that is not navigation has to be a button - so a button.link rendered at 13.3px inside 14px text with 1px 6px of padding and an outset border. font-weight is untouched so .quiet/.standalone still decide it, and display stays inline-block. Scoped with :where(), so the reset sits at .link specificity and a consumer rule still wins on source order.

DELETE-LIST: if you have a local .link-button class, or a padding/border/background/font reset on button.link in your overrides -> .link ships it now. mm-broker carried exactly those four lines after replacing three near-duplicate local classes with "link sm standalone".

ds-stat gained --ds-stat-value-white-space and --ds-stat-value-font-size, both defaulting to what the tile already rendered (nowrap, and h2/h4/h1 by size), so no existing tile moves. They exist because a value that is a PHRASE - a date range, a status - spilled straight past the tile edge under the nowrap that suits a number - the card sets no overflow, so it is not clipped, it escapes. The size hook now applies at every size input: the sm and lg variants move this token instead of restating font-size on .value, where they out-ranked any override and made such a hook work at md only.

DELETE-LIST: if you projected into ds-stat [dsStatValue] only to set white-space: normal or a smaller font-size on a text value -> the two hooks do it on the ordinary value input, and the tile keeps its geometry either way. Keep the slot for a value that is genuinely another component, like a badge.

ds-search takes [debounce] (milliseconds, default 0). At 0 it writes value on every keystroke exactly as before, so nothing changes until you ask. THREE things deliberately skip the timer, which is what a wrapped debounceTime usually gets wrong: emptying the field, the Clear button, and Enter - the last flushing a keystroke still in flight so `submitted` carries what the reader can see. Emptying also cancels a pending keystroke, so a fast type-then-clear cannot land the stale query afterwards. What the input SHOWS is never delayed at any setting, and a host writing value mid-typing wins and cancels the timer.

DELETE-LIST: if you wrapped ds-search to add a debounce - typically 200ms on typing with an immediate path when the field empties -> [debounce] does both, plus the Enter flush. mm-broker carried exactly that wrapper for exactly those two behaviours.

ds-filter-bar no longer clips the focus ring of its first and last inline filter. The measured row was overflow: hidden with each slot sized to exactly its declared width, so the row box started flush with the first control while the ring is an OUTSET shadow (3px on fields, 4px on controls) - interior filters were fine in the 12px gap, the outer two were cut off as you tabbed onto them. Now overflow: clip with a 4px clip margin; clip still forbids scrolling, so the width the collapse arithmetic reads is unchanged. Nothing to do, and it was not fixable from an app: the row is internal and padding it from outside would have changed that measured width.

ds-filter-bar takes triggerSize (sm|md|lg, default md) for its own "+N" trigger. The bar cannot infer it: dsFilterItem carries a WIDTH and the filters are arbitrary projected controls whose size it never sees, so a row of sm filters got an md trigger standing 8px taller under align-items: flex-end. DELETE-LIST: if you pinned --ds-button-height / --ds-button-font-size / --ds-button-pad-x under ds-filter-bar to force the trigger smaller -> triggerSize="sm" replaces all three.

If you must hold two trailing controls in ONE component, the Filter bar page now shows the three declarations its :host owes (display: flex; align-items: flex-end; gap: var(--ds-filter-bar-gap, var(--space-3))) - the bar's own trailing rule, with the gap read from the existing public token so the copy cannot drift. The usual REASON for pairing them is also gone: a bar-level Clear no longer has to share a component with the search to cancel an armed debounce, because ds-search cancels its own pending keystroke when the host writes value.

DS_CONFIG gained a modal section: provideDsConfig({ modal: { dividers: false } }) sets the default for ds-modal and ds-modal-card app-wide, or on a route or subtree, with an explicit [dividers] on the element still winning. It reaches where an attribute cannot - a ModalService confirm renders a ds-modal-card with no ds-modal ancestor to bind - which is why a per-element input was not enough. Internally [dividers] is now boolean | null so "unset" stays distinguishable from an explicit false; existing bindings are unaffected.

DELETE-LIST: if you repeat [dividers]="false" on every modal (mm-broker has 41), or reach into .modal > .header|.body|.actions with !important because hiding the rules left the padding stacked -> provideDsConfig({ modal: { dividers: false } }) replaces both. Which padding collapses is deliberate: the BODY drops to zero and the header/actions keep theirs, because the body is the scroll container and a gap in its padding would scroll away and let content meet the title.

ds-tabs takes rememberLastTab (off by default), which reopens the tab a screen was last left on. Stored per path in sessionStorage under ds-tabs:{path}:{param}; inert without urlParam, which supplies the names because a remembered INDEX would repoint the moment a tab is inserted. A link always wins - the query parameter is read first and memory only fills the gap the first tab deliberately leaves. Every storage access is guarded, so Safari private mode simply means the strip stops remembering. DELETE-LIST: a helper that kept the last tab per path in sessionStorage can go.

DS_CONFIG gained a brand section: provideDsConfig({ brand: { name, logoLetter, tagline } }) answers ds-sidenav and ds-auth-layout together, since both take the same three and an app answers them identically on every screen. Each field resolves independently - an element input beats the config per FIELD, so overriding the name does not mean restating the letter, and brand="" drops the wordmark while a logoLetter in the config still paints its tile (clear both for no brand row). The two-tone wordmark is deliberately NOT in the config: [dsBrandName] stays the accent's home, because a config string would have to be split apart to find the accent, and the projection wins over both. Shape: brand, logoLetter and tagline are now string | null with a null default so "unset" is distinguishable from an explicit empty; the input names did not change and template bindings are unaffected.

DELETE-LIST: if you wrote an adapter component that injects a brand object and fans it out into brand/logoLetter/tagline bindings on each auth screen -> provideDsConfig({ brand: … }) does it, and the accent stays a [dsBrandName] projection instead of a brandAccent string plus an indexOf split.

ds-avatar takes a `name`, which replaces the two bindings a caller used to wire by hand: it derives the initials AND seeds the tint. The tint hashes the NAME rather than the initials - two letters collide wholesale, so Alice Brown and Adam Bell would otherwise share a colour (measured: same "AB", hues 198 and 356). An explicit `initials` still wins, and `seed` still overrides the hash input when identity is an id or an email rather than the display name.

The rule turning a name into initials is REPLACEABLE rather than configurable by mode: [initialsRule] on one avatar or table, provideDsConfig({ avatar: { initials } }) for the app. The built-in stays initialsFrom - first two words - and is documented as a Latin-script guess, because reading a name is a cultural convention rather than a UI decision: a Spanish reader wants MG from "Maria Jose Garcia Lopez", an insurer wants BC from "Blue Cross Blue Shield". A library that shipped person/organisation modes would be claiming to know both, and would be wrong in ways it cannot see. DELETE-LIST: local initials helpers stay yours, but the ds-avatar wiring around them collapses to [name] plus one [initialsRule].

ds-multi-select and ds-autocomplete render an option's `icon` before its label at 16px, which previously only ds-select did. The three option types now extend one exported DsOption<T> - they were three near-identical interfaces, which is why the icon field existed on one picker for a release - and each keeps its own exported name, so no import changes. Nothing to do: options without an icon render as before. Only ds-select repeats the icon in its TRIGGER, because its trigger is a button showing one label; the autocomplete trigger is a text input whose leading slot belongs to [dsAutocompletePrefix], and multi-select chips stay text-only so the label keeps the width.

provideDsConfig gained five sections, so an app can state a whole-app opinion once instead of on every element: control.size (button, icon-button, input, textarea, select, autocomplete, search, date/time picker, number stepper, checkbox, radio, switch, field-group), card.elevation, card.padding, table.stickyScrollbar, table.bordered, icon.size and badge.withDot. Precedence is input -> config -> built-in, and NO built-in default moved: an app that provides nothing renders exactly as it did. DELETE-LIST: the attribute you repeat identically on every element - one consumer binds [stickyScrollbar]="true" on all 35 of its tables and size="sm" on 146 buttons.

DS_CONFIG.control.size is NOT the same axis as [data-density]. The density tier rewrites hit targets and padding in CSS for a route subtree; control.size picks which of the three declared sizes (sm/md/lg) a control renders at. An app can set both, and they compose.

MEASURED IN A CONSUMER, worth checking on your own side: 46 of its ds-icon elements bind [size]="16", which is already the ds-icon default - dead bindings, not a gap. Config or no config, those can go.
